record.paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
record.context_brief: Variable-coefficient and semilinear half-line heat equations
record.original_question: Consider the one-dimensional variable-coefficient heat equation on the half-line p(x)u_t − (a(x)u_x)_x = 0 for x>0 and t>0, with boundary control u(0,t)=v(t) and initial datum u(x,0)=u_0(x), where a and p are positive, bounded, smooth functions. Determine whether the lack of null-controllability proved in the chapter for the constant-coefficient half-line heat equation extends to this more general variable-coefficient setting. More generally, determine whether the same negative phenomenon persists for equations whose coefficients depend on both x and t, for equations with lower-order potentials, or for semilinear variants on the half-line.

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to see if the negative results of Section 3 may be extended to this more general equation (with, say, a and p positive, bounded and smooth functions).
Of course, the same problem arises for more general equations: coefficients depending both on x and t, equations with lower order potentials, equations involving semilinear terms, ....

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional heat equation on the half-line with variable coefficients:
  p(x) u_t(x,t) − (a(x) u_x(x,t))_x = 0,   x > 0, t ∈ (0,T),
with boundary control u(0,t) = v(t), t ∈ (0,T), and initial datum u(x,0) = u_0(x), x > 0, where a, p : (0,∞) → ℝ are positive, bounded, smooth functions and v ∈ L^2(0,T) is the control.

The system is said to be null-controllable at time T from the initial datum u_0 if there exists a control v ∈ L^2(0,T) such that the corresponding solution satisfies u(·,T) ≡ 0 on (0,∞). It is known that for the constant-coefficient case (a ≡ p ≡ 1), null-controllability fails: there exist initial data u_0 ∈ L^2(0,∞) that cannot be steered to 0 in any time T > 0 by any L^2 boundary control.

Questions:
(a) Does this lack of null-controllability persist for every choice of positive, bounded, smooth coefficients a(x), p(x)?
(b) Does the same negative phenomenon hold when the coefficients depend on both x and t, i.e. a = a(x,t), p = p(x,t)?
(c) Does it hold in the presence of a lower-order potential, i.e. for equations of the form p(x) u_t − (a(x) u_x)_x + c(x,t) u = 0?
(d) Does it hold for semilinear variants p(x) u_t − (a(x) u_x)_x + f(u) = 0 on the half-line, under suitable growth assumptions on f?
artifact.status_search_result: The constant-coefficient lack of null-controllability on the half-line (Micu–Zuazua, 2001) has been re-proved by elementary/Fokas-method arguments (e.g., 2019/2020). Positive controllability results are available on bounded domains with variable coefficients, but a definitive extension of the half-line negative result to general variable coefficients a(x), p(x), to (x,t)-dependent coefficients, to lower-order potentials, or to semilinear variants does not appear to be established in the literature found. The status thus appears unresolved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: An elementary proof of the lack of null controllability for the heat equation on the half line
status_evidence.snippet: Elementary proof, via Fokas method, of the lack of null-controllability for the constant-coefficient heat equation on the half line.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the constant-coefficient negative result; does not address general variable coefficients on the half line.

status_evidence.title: Null Controllability and Finite Time Stabilization for the Heat Equations with Variable Coefficients in Space in One Dimension via Backstepping Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Variable-coefficient null controllability is established in bounded one-dimensional domains via backstepping.
status_evidence.claim: Variable-coefficient positive results are for bounded intervals, not the half-line.
